inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.constructor.state
inputs.description: Durable Object state retained by the adapter to accept sockets and enumerate sockets held by the runtime, including after hibernation.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.open.attachment
inputs.description: Identity and closed flag serialized on the new server socket; its role and IDs also determine the tags used by later lookups.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.attachment.socket
inputs.description: The runtime-held WebSocket whose serialized attachment is read. Callers use it to recover socket identity after hibernation.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.device.deviceId
inputs.description: Exact device identifier appended to the `device:` tag when selecting that device's live sockets; the adapter does not normalize it.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.connection.connectionId
inputs.description: Exact connection identifier appended to the `connection:` tag when selecting its live socket; the adapter does not normalize it.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.send.socket
inputs.description: The target WebSocket for a JSON text frame. The method attempts send without checking readyState and returns false if serialization or send throws.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.send.frame
inputs.description: The value JSON-stringified and sent as one text frame. Serialization or send failures make the operation return false.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.close.socket
inputs.description: The WebSocket to close. If its attachment exists, the adapter first marks it closed so live lookups stop returning it.

inputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.close.code
inputs.description: The close code passed to WebSocket.close; an error from closing is swallowed by the adapter.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.open
outputs.description: The pair for a newly accepted connection: the client endpoint and server endpoint registered with the Durable Object, tagged and attached for later lookup.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.attachment
outputs.description: The socket's deserialized SocketAttachment, or undefined when no attachment is stored; callers use it to identify its host or device connection.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.host
outputs.description: The first live socket tagged `host`, or undefined when none is available. A socket counts only while OPEN and attached with `closed: false`.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.devices
outputs.description: All sockets tagged `device` that are OPEN and have an attachment with `closed: false`.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.device
outputs.description: All OPEN sockets tagged `device:<deviceId>` whose attachments have `closed: false`; the supplied ID must match the tag exactly.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.connection
outputs.description: The first OPEN socket tagged `connection:<connectionId>` with an attachment marked `closed: false`, or undefined when none remains active.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.all
outputs.description: Every WebSocket still held by the Durable Object, including sockets that are closing or excluded from live lookups.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.send
outputs.description: True when JSON serialization and socket.send complete; false when either throws. The adapter does not queue a frame for later.

outputs.name: HostSocketsAdapter.close
outputs.description: No return value. The adapter marks an existing attachment closed, then calls WebSocket.close with reason `closed`; socket errors are ignored.

errors.name: Workers runtime error
errors.description: open does not catch errors from the runtime's acceptWebSocket and serializeAttachment calls, for example an attachment over the runtime's attachment size limit. send and close catch every error.
